decisions.why: Two changes bind this board: (1) board-wide HV clearance raised 0.60 -> 0.635 mm per TPS2378 vendor layout guidance, daughters inherit it; (2) new s8.4 - the carrier's TPS16630 load switch has a mandatory 10k SHDN pull-down, so a daughter may assume an unprogrammed/crashed/reset/brownout carrier presents 0 V at J3, not 48 V. decisions.what: LED stage stays on +12V (baseline); the P1 '48V is 16x better for dimming slew' argument is WITHDRAWN as an artifact of holding L fixed
decisions.why: Verified algebraically by the orchestrator: with L sized for the same ripple fraction k, t_rise+t_fall = 1/(f*k), independent of Vin. At 700 kHz / k=0.30 both rails give 4.762 us (48V only redistributes 3.81/0.95 us between rise and fall). That is 33.8x the 141 ns PAR-REQ-01 budget, so NO rail or inductor choice reaches the requirement by gating the converter - it needs shunt-FET dimming either way. The 48V branch therefore buys nothing on fidelity and costs 0.635 mm creepage, 100 V caps, bleed path and daughter-owned inrush.

decisions.what: Stackup JLC04161H-3313, 4 layers, 100.0 x 80.0 mm, 1.6 mm
decisions.why: Switch-node containment 11 mm above a live 2.4 GHz antenna (H1-Q8 made Wi-Fi a supported control path), continuous GND reference under jitter-sensitive PWM, B.Cu consumed by two reverse-mounted sockets, ~120 parts in ~45 cm2. No controlled-impedance net exists on this board.

decisions.what: Dimming topology: shunt FET per channel across the LED string
decisions.why: Closes the PAR-REQ-01 TIMING wall: TPS92515HV direct PWM floors at 200 ns vs a 141 ns requirement, but its shunt mode is spec'd 10,000:1 = 10.2 ns min pulse. Implemented T ~ 50-100 ns, 1.4-2.8x margin. The RESOLUTION wall (17 bits needed, LEDC caps at 14) is NOT closable on this board and needs carrier firmware dithering (CR-5).

decisions.what: Design point 150 mA/die, 4 emitter packages, 2S2P per channel; emitters off-board on aluminium MCPCB
decisions.why: Full white = 0.718 A on +12V, 4 % under the sustained ceiling and 2.8x under OCP, so the board is electrically incapable of exceeding its budget with every PWM stuck at 100 %. Off-board MCPCB because 1.6 mm FR4 misses the junction budget by 2-3x. >3 A conditional flag CLOSED (max 0.30 A/channel).

decisions.what: No fifth (amber) channel on rev A; fit BOTH ID mechanisms (ID_ADC bottom-leg divider + I2C EEPROM)
decisions.why: Amber dilutes an af envelope that full white already fills to 96 % of the rail ceiling. ICD s3.3 makes the divider and the EEPROM coexist rather than alternatives - the divider gives board type, the EEPROM per-unit calibration - so PAR-REQ-17 is met without spending a pin.

decisions.what: Q3 CLOSED: PAR-REQ-01 met by hardware + firmware. Strict reading (5% perceived, gamma 2.2) binds.
decisions.why: Carrier firmware commits to PWM-domain dithering >=3-4 bits (CR-5 accepted). Shunt-FET hardware half stands as designed (T ~50-100 ns vs 141 ns). decisions.what: Sense resistor 0.75 ohm (not 0.68), nominal 275 mA/channel - the COMPLIANT value is the default
decisions.why: P3 found that 0.68 ohm with IADJ tied to VCC gives a +-5.6% threshold band -> ILED 284-324 mA -> 0.775 A worst case = 103% of the ICD 0.75 A +12V sustained ceiling. Orchestrator reproduced it and also costed the proposed IADJ divider: the divider tightens the band but lowers the threshold too, landing at essentially the same light (0.928 vs 0.917 of nominal) for 8 extra resistors - REJECTED. Compliant-by-construction is the right default because the stuck-PWM backstop is exactly the case where firmware is dead and cannot govern the average. Costs 8.3% light vs the H1 point. Reversible: BOM value only, zero layout impact, changeable to P9. Flagged for H2.

decisions.what: Shunt FET switched to TOSHIBA SSM3K2615R,LXGF (C22371361, SOT-23F)
decisions.why: Closes two P3 open items at once. Ciss 150 pF into the 150 R gate resistor is tau ~22 ns, so gate edges land in the tens of ns against PAR-REQ-01's 141 ns pulse - the previously selected part was estimated at 100-140 ns, which would have eaten the entire timing budget. And Rds(on) 580 mohm is specified AT 3.3 V, so it is guaranteed on at our gate drive rather than inferred. Also resolves the no-first-tier-brand-in-stock risk. Dissipation 69 mW at 0.345 A peak. Package is SOT-23F not SOT-23 - fp_verify needs extra attention.

decisions.why: ICD s5.2 derives its 0.84 mm pad-to-pad creepage from the THT land pattern (1.70 mm annulus on a 1.02 mm drill), and that geometry is the carrier owner's frozen number. An SMD land pattern changes it and would require the ICD to be re-issued. Two hand-solder operations across 8 boards is the cheaper side of that trade.

decisions.what: Re-synced ICD copy again; daughters MUST use a 1.70 mm annulus on the connector pads (1.10 mm drill, 0.300 mm/side ring)
decisions.why: The carrier's P3 library work corrected the drill from the assumed 1.02 mm to an actual 1.10 mm, and normalised J3's annulus from 1.80 to 1.70 mm so both frozen connectors share one land pattern. The 0.84 mm pad-to-pad gap and the 1.32x clearance conclusion are unchanged, but the annulus is now an explicit daughter requirement - this is a librarian/fp_verify checkpoint, not just a note.

decisions.why: Coordinator: 'a margin that only holds while software works is not a margin.' Reversion to 0.68 ohm stays live as a one-code swap through P9.

decisions.what: CR-1 CLOSED: R206 = 4.7 kOhm, 1% REQUIRED (not preferred). LUM-PAR-A is ID_ADC code 2, V_ID = 1.055 V.
decisions.why: ICD s3.4 rev A3, NORMATIVE. Verified: 3.3 x 4700/(4700+10000) = 1.0551 V. 1% is required because adjacent-code separation is 0.353 V against a +-0.05 V divider error from 1% parts plus a +-0.15 V firmware window - a 5% part eats the margin. Cited by section+amendment revision, not the header (the header reads A3 while its own parenthetical lists amendments through A6). The strobe run found its placeholder was set to THIS board's code and would have shipped announcing itself as the par - the value is functional, not cosmetic.

decisions.what: CR-6 CLOSED by ICD s7.7 rev A5 (NORMATIVE): sealed + wall-conducted, internal air 32-33 C at a 25 C room
decisions.why: The carrier re-derived and reconciled. With the LED wall path WORKING only 1.894 W enters box air (6.8-8.1 K rise); with it FAILING 8.5 W enters and gives 56-62 C - which reproduces the rev A2 af figure to the degree. So the af number was never miscalculated, it was the LED-heat-stays-in-box case at a 25 C room with NEITHER assumption written down. The at figure WAS a genuine error, exactly as this run found. This run's 89-115 C Hoffman/Rittal figure is now recorded as the CONSERVATIVE BOUND and the ICD explicitly says do not average it. Budget: 10.5-12.5 W of box air at a 25 C room holding air to 70 C.

decisions.what: PWM allocation NORMATIVE (ICD s3.5 rev A3): LUM-PAR-A runs PWM0-3 on ONE timer, 13-bit / 9.766 kHz, with a 90 degree phase stagger. CR-3 (14-bit/4.883 kHz) is GRANTED and available opt-in; CR-4 (stagger) is GRANTED.
decisions.why: The prior ICD claim that PWM0-3 sit on timer 0 and PWM4-7 on timer 1 is WITHDRAWN - the carrier does not hard-assign timers; each daughter declares its own map and firmware applies it from the ID_ADC code. Three timers remain free for this board. The 14-bit option doubles the driver timing budget from 141 ns to 281 ns and makes firmware dithering physically reproducible - it costs camera-flicker margin and must be re-tested against a phone camera on the first prototype.

decisions.what: ADOPT the 14-bit / 4.883 kHz PWM mode (CR-3, granted) as this board declared timer map, instead of 13-bit / 9.766 kHz
decisions.why: It doubles the driver timing budget from 141 ns to 281 ns, which converts the shunt-FET timing risk from unverified-and-probably-violated into comfortable margin against the only switching number that exists (toff 150 ns typ). It ALSO doubles the LSB duration, which is what makes firmware PWM-domain dithering physically reproducible - spec-dimming s2.7 ranks 1 and 2 as a package, not alternatives. Cost is camera-flicker margin: band contrast rises from 0.61% to 1.23% at 60 fps (still under the visibility threshold) and 2.46% to 4.92% at 240 fps - and H1-P9 already recommends declaring 240 fps out of scope. ICD s3.5 makes the mode opt-in per daughter and requires a phone-camera re-test on the first prototype.

decisions.what: The power sheet owns ALL FOUR PWR_FLAGs (GND, +12V, +3V3, +48V_SW); every other sheet places consuming power symbols only

decisions.what: J5 entry-direction question CLOSED: S10B-PH-SM4-TB is SIDE ENTRY and is the CORRECT part - no swap-part
decisions.why: datasheet p3 splits the model table into Top entry (B2B..B16B-PH-SM4-TB) and Side entry (S2B..S15B-PH-SM4-TB) columns, repeated twice more for the THT and LIF variants: the entry code is the LEADING letter, and the B in '10B' appears in every model of the series. Side entry is also right for this board - the module mounts to the enclosure wall so the harness leaves laterally regardless, and J5 is on B.Cu inside the ICD's 11.0 mm mezzanine gap where a top-entry PHR-10 housing plus bend radius would foul the carrier

decisions.what: The /PWM0..3 nets MUST carry the canonical root-level names /PWM0../PWM3; preferred mechanism is exposing them as hierarchical pins from control, with re-spelling constraints.json to /control/PWMn as the sanctioned fallback if that is not ERC-clean
decisions.why: sheets.md s2 states these are the names the schematic must produce, and constraints.json.high_speed feeds SEVEN consumers (check_return_path, planes_gen, route_critical, rules_gen, stitch_vias, constraints_lint, netlist_audit) - a mismatch silently drops the jitter-sensitive PWM nets from every one of them, on the board whose hardest requirement is the PAR-REQ-01 141 ns timing wall. It also fails netlist_audit outright (missing_net is an error), so it must be settled before the root build. sheets.md is internally inconsistent here - it lists PWM in the INTERFACE net table while its own From->to column calls them control-internal - so the tie-break is which artifact ends up TRUE: name-match is required either way, and the hier-pin route keeps one uniform convention across all root nets

decisions.what: REVERSAL of the earlier P4 ruling: /PWM0..3 keep their real netlist names /control/PWM0..3, and constraints.json high_speed was re-spelled to match. The preferred hier-pin mechanism was tried, measured and REJECTED
decisions.why: the hier-pin route works electrically (netlist carried /PWM0 = J4-1 + R202-1 + U202-1) but is NOT ERC-clean: 4x label_dangling, because the root subgraph for those nets is wire + label + exactly ONE sheet pin and KiCad 10.0.3 requires a real connection point. Two probes settled the rule: a second same-named root label does NOT satisfy it (8 errors, both flagged), while one TestPoint pin per root PWM wire takes the identical project to 0/0 - so buying the bare name would mean adding four PARTS to the root, a design change rather than a stitch fix. Every other root net escapes this only because two children expose it. lumina-carrier never exercised it: all 70 of its root labels appear 2-3 times. Outcome is equivalent for the seven high_speed consumers, which match on exact name and do not validate name shape

decisions.what: H2: emitter-hot hysteresis band ACCEPTED at 8.6 K (trip 89.9 C, release 81.2 C) against a 15 K aspiration; R207 stays 100k
decisions.why: trip is exact on spec at 89.9 C and only the release sits high. Widening needs a smaller feedback resistor, which trades directly against the emitter-OPEN channel margin - and emitter-open is the fail-safe that catches the broken harness this block exists for. Board-hot is already on spec at 110.2/92.9. The R207 route was recommended against and rejected: the thermal rework removed its justification (released FAULT now >=2.81 V in every corner incl. unmated-hot, which used to sag to 1.80 V below U201 VIH) and a stronger pull-up would shift every trip point, forcing a full MNA re-solve for no remaining benefit
